content.title: Recap: Skubal dominates, McGonigle shines in debut as Tigers dominate Padres
content.text: Updated March 26, 2026, 7:09 p.m. ETThe Detroit Tigers open their 2026 season on Thursday with a 4:10 p.m. first pitch against the Padres at Petco Park in San Diego. Follow the action here with live updates throughout the game by Detroit News contributor Kameron Goodwill. Final: Tigers 8, Padres 2For the second year in a row, the Tigers went to the west coast to open their season against a NL West team. But this time, they came out victorious with a dominant 8-2 victory over the Padres.It was a day that Tigers rookie Kevin McGonigle will never forget. Not only did he record his first major league hit, he finished 4-for-5 with two doubles and two RBIs. His first hit, swinging at the first pitch, was a double that scored two runs to give the Tigers a 3-0 lead in the first inning. The Tigers overall had 12 hits, seven of those going against Padres starter Nick Pivetta who allowed six runs in just three innings pitched.Tarik Skubal proved why he's a back-to-back Cy Young winner. In six innings, he got six strikeouts and allowed just one run on three hits, including four straight innings without allowing a single runner on base after allowing two hits in the first inning. The Tigers play the Padres two more times in San Diego and have their first six games against NL West opponents. Skubal, McGonigle shine as Tigers dominate Padres in opener victoryWandy Peralta comes in as the final pitcher for the Padres today, getting Greene and Torkelson to fly out. But yet again, it's McGonigle with a single to center field for his fourth hit today! Unfortunately, Dingler grounds out to end the top of the ninth.Will Vest comes in to close out this opening game, and he does it by getting three straight outs, finishing it out by striking out Cronenworth as the Tigers cruise to an impressive Opening Day win. Tigers, Padres both threaten to score in eighth but no runs come in, Detroit still leads 8-2Fourth pitcher comes in for the Padres as David Morgan comes to the mound, and he starts off by getting Meadows to pop-out for the first out, then walks Báez in five pitches. Carpenter also strikes out, but Torres gets on the board with a single to center field, moving Báez to third base. Keith hits a liner but it's right to Cronenworth for the third out.Anderson stays on the mound for the bottom of the eighth as Tatís hits a single to center field, but Bogaerts lines out to Greene for the first out. Machado is walked in four pitches and a mound visit is taken with a timeout, as Tyler Holton takes over with one out. Merrill hits a grounder but the Tigers can only get the out at second base, then Holton walks Andujart to load the bases. Former Tiger Nick Castellanos pinch-hits but flies out to center field to end the eighth inning. Skubal leaves after impressive start, Padres score again but Tigers still lead, 8-2, after seven innings.Rodriguez continues his strong relief appearance, as Torkelson strikes out for the second time today, then McGonigle finally gets out for the first time today on a pop-out, then Dingler lines out for the final out of the top of the seventh inning.Skubal's day is done as Drew Anderson takes over, and he starts off strong by getting Andujar to ground out and Sheets to pop out, but the Laureano hits a fly ball deep to left field and it's gone for a home run. Fermin takes a six-pitch walk as Anderson gets a quick mound visit, and it works as he gets Cronenworth to ground out, ending the seventh inning.Final stats for Skubal's 2026 Opening Day start: six innings pitched, three hits and one run allowed with six strikeouts and no walks allowed for a dominant performance. Padres finally score, Tigers still hold 8-1 lead after six inningsIn case anyone's wondering, Skubal is a pretty good pitcher. The Padres haven't put a hit against him since the first inning, and it continues in the bottom of the fifth as Gavin Sheets grounds out while Laureano and Freddy Fermin fly out for three easy outs.Bradgley Rodriguez is the third pitcher for the Padres today to start the top of the sixth, as the Tigers can't get a hit and Rodriguez pitches a three up, three down inning for just the second time out of this Padres pitching. In the bottom of the sixth, Skubal's still on the mound and Tatís gets to first base after Torkelson is led away from the base on a throwing error, the first person allowed on base for the Tigers since the first inning.After review confirms the call, Bogaerts gets a hit down the left-field line as Tatís scores from first for a RBI-double and the first run for the Padres today. But Skubal recovers with back-to-back strikeouts on Machado and Merrill to end the sixth inning. McGonigle gets his third hit, Dingler's dinger brings Tigers' lead to 8-0 in fifth inningSkubal's in midseason form as he gets Machado to fly out, strikes out Merrill, and gets Andujar to fly out for three outs in just seven pitches, as that ends the fourth inning.Marianaccio strikes out Torkelson in just five pitches, then McGonigle hustles as he beats out the throw to first base for his third hit of the day! And the runs just keep coming, as Dingler takes a ball deep to left center field for a home run, the first of the Tigers' season and it's now 8-0 Detroit. The Tigers don't score anymore runs, but this lead has ballooned up. Skubal keeps Padres at-bay, Pivetta leaves after three innings pitched and six runs given upSkubal continues to cruise against this Padres lineup, as Jake Cronenworth lines out followed by Tatís popping out. Greene makes an amazing catch on the warning track for the last out of the third inning.In the top of the fourth, Pivetta's day is done as reliever Ron Marianaccio comes in to pitch for the Padres and he gets both Torres and Keith to ground out and Greene strikes out. McGonigle gets second hit, Tigers take 6-0 lead in third inningTorkelson fights off Pivetta for an eight-pitch walk, then McGonigle gets a hit off the right-field wall for his second hit and second double of the day! Dingler strikes out swinging for the first out, but Meadows gets a ball to drop in center field to score two more runs and the Tigers are out to a 6-0 lead.Pivetta stays pitching after another mound visit, as Báez pops out and Carpenter flies out to end this frame. Skubal's up to 3 Ks so far, Tigers still hold 4-0 leadThe top of the second inning goes scoreless for the Tigers, as only Colt Keith gets a hit off of Pivetta while the Tigers' three outs come from three fly outs.In the bottom of the second, Skubal gets Gavin Sheets to ground out, while throwing back-to-back strikeouts on Ramón Laureano and Freddy Fermin as he's up to three strikeouts already. Skubal allows two hits, no runs as first inning endsTarik Skubal takes the mound for his first start this season, as he gets Fernando Tatís Jr. to ground out, then Xander Bogaerts and Manny Machado hit back-to-back singles to put runners on first and third. But Skubal gets out of the jam as he gets Jackson Merill to strike out and Miguel Andujar grounds out to leave runners stranded and no runs scored. McGonigle gets first major league hit, helps Tigers take 4-0 lead in first inning of season openerFirst pitch is thrown at 4:12 p.m. as Kerry Carpenter hits it to foul territory against Padres starting pitcher Nick Pivetta, then Pivetta gets Carpenter to strike out in three pitches. Gleyber Torres draws a walk in five pitches, then Colt Keith gets a ball to drop in left field for the first hit of the Tigers' 2026 season. Pivetta then walks Riley Greene to load the bases with one out.After a mound visit, Spencer Torkelson draws a walk as the Tigers score their first run of the season. It doesn't stop there as Kevin McGonigle swings at the first pitch and its a liner down right field, bringing two runners home for his first major league hit and a 3-0 Tigers lead. Dillon Dingler hits a grounder to score another run, then both Parker Meadows and Javier Báez strike out as the Tigers take a 4-0 lead. How to watch the Tigers vs. Padres openerAll three games of the Tigers' season-opening series against the Padres – Thursday, Friday and Saturday – are on Detroit SportsNet, which is being delivered through MLB Media.Detroit SportsNet is available on Xfinity, Spectrum, DirecTV and Fubo. Fans can find their channels at tigers.com/watch. Tigers games can also be streamed by purchasing a subscription at tigers.com/DetroitSportsNet.
